title: Zaara and Akrofi Share the Poster

pages.text: Zaara and Akrofi were drawing a science poster about plants. “We must use green!” said Akrofi. “No, blue!” said Zaara. Their voices grew louder and louder until classmates nearby stopped working to stare.
sentences: Zaara and Akrofi were drawing a science poster about plants.
“We must use green!” said Akrofi.
“No, blue!” said Zaara.
Their voices grew louder and louder until classmates nearby stopped working to stare.
pages.alt: At a shared classroom table, Akrofi holds up a green marker and Zaara holds up a blue marker with cross faces over a large blank sheet of paper while classmates look over.

pages.text: Zaara stopped. She closed her eyes, took a slow, deep breath, and counted to five. “I feel cross,” she thought, “yet shouting will not help.” Her heart slowed down, and her mind felt clearer.
sentences: Zaara stopped.
She closed her eyes, took a slow, deep breath, and counted to five.
“I feel cross,” she thought, “yet shouting will not help.” Her heart slowed down, and her mind felt clearer.
pages.alt: Close view of Zaara with her eyes gently closed and one hand resting calmly over her chest as she takes a slow, steadying breath.

pages.text: Calmly, she said, “Akrofi, I feel upset when we both shout. I would like us to listen to each other.” Akrofi blinked in surprise; he had expected more shouting. Slowly, he lowered his shoulders and nodded.
sentences: Calmly, she said, “Akrofi, I feel upset when we both shout.
I would like us to listen to each other.” Akrofi blinked in surprise; he had expected more shouting.
Slowly, he lowered his shoulders and nodded.
pages.alt: Zaara speaking calmly with open hands to Akrofi across the poster paper while Akrofi lowers his marker and nods thoughtfully.

pages.text: Zaara listened carefully first. “I chose green because leaves and stems are green,” explained Akrofi. Then Akrofi listened. “I chose blue because rain and rivers give plants water,” said Zaara. Both reasons were good.
sentences: Zaara listened carefully first.
“I chose green because leaves and stems are green,” explained Akrofi.
Then Akrofi listened.
“I chose blue because rain and rivers give plants water,” said Zaara.
Both reasons were good.
pages.alt: Akrofi and Zaara leaning across their desk in friendly conversation, listening respectfully to each other’s ideas.

pages.text: They thought of three choices: green only, blue only, or using both colours together. Smiling, they chose both—Akrofi drew lush green leaves and stems, while Zaara added bright blue raindrops and a flowing stream.
sentences: They thought of three choices: green only, blue only, or using both colours together.
Smiling, they chose both—Akrofi drew lush green leaves and stems, while Zaara added bright blue raindrops and a flowing stream.
pages.alt: Overhead classroom view of Zaara and Akrofi happily colouring one vibrant picture-only plant drawing together with green leaves and blue raindrops.

pages.text: Madam Salamatu smiled proudly as they hung their artwork on the wall. “You solved that wisely,” she said. “Whenever we disagree, we can stop, breathe, say how we feel, listen, think of choices, and choose together.”

pages.alt: Zaara and Akrofi smiling side by side beside their colourful plant artwork on the classroom wall while Madam Salamatu applauds warmly.

activities.question: What did Zaara do first to calm down?
options: Stopped, breathed slowly, and counted to five

activities.question: How did Zaara and Akrofi settle their disagreement?

activities.prompt: Put the peace-making steps in order.
items: Stop and take a slow breath.
Say how you feel without shouting.
Listen carefully to the other person.
Think of choices and choose together.

activities.prompt: How do you feel when you and a friend solve a disagreement kindly?

glossary.definition: A large picture sheet made to share an idea on a wall.
To hold a different idea or wish from someone else.
To pay quiet, careful attention to what someone is saying.
